$comment: BUCKET B — everything client-specific, as data rather than code. The engine (src/lib/kb/fts) and the product logic (src/lib/kb/gate.ts) contain no NimbusStack knowledge at all. Onboarding a second client is a new file in this directory plus its own corpus and eval/<client>.jsonl — not a new branch of the retriever.

corpus.$productTitleComment: How a document declares which product it belongs to. Still inferred from an H1 here because this corpus is hand-written markdown. The moment a Confluence export or a PDF arrives this must become DECLARED metadata (frontmatter or a sidecar manifest) — a page titled 'Vault - Pricing (FY26)' yields no product, which silently disables scoping and makes a Vault question answerable from Pulse's documents. The builder refuses to index a dateless or productless chunk silently; see requireProduct.
corpus.$requireProductComment: false while the corpus is hand-written and 4 of 10 files are legitimately company-wide. Flip to true the day ingestion is automated, so a parse failure quarantines a document instead of indexing it unscoped.
corpus.$brandTermsComment: Excluded from topical terms exactly as product names are. The company's own name says 'this question is about us', not 'this is the topic' — counting it as topical evidence let 'who is the CEO of NimbusStack' and 'tell me about Nimbus Forge' clear the refusal gate on the brand alone.

$fieldWeightComment: Real BM25F per-field weighting, passed to bm25(). This replaces repeating the heading three times into the token stream — which inflated the document length and so partly cancelled, through BM25's length normalisation, the boost it was meant to create.
$stopwordComment: LANGUAGE-LEVEL English function words (src/lib/kb/stopwords.ts), not a per-corpus list. The original plan was to derive these from corpus document frequency, and that is MEASURABLY WRONG at this corpus's shape: df/N >= 0.5 yields only 2 useless terms, and by df/N >= 0.3 the rule has already removed 'pro', 'enterpris' and 'saml' — the tier names and subject matter every pricing and SSO question turns on. Document frequency cannot tell a function word from a topic word. dfRatio below is therefore a BUILD DIAGNOSTIC only: the build prints which terms are corpus-wide boilerplate, and nothing filters on it. `extra` is the per-client escape hatch and should stay empty.
$identComment: Typed identifiers, extracted at index time into a table and matched exactly, rather than hoped-for in a tokenizer. Every exact-token failure in the previous design was a token-matching failure against a value that is really a typed entity: 'v4.2' tokenised whole and never matched the heading '4.2', so 'what changed in Relay v4.2' was refused outright. These are structured data; FTS5's tokenizer never sees them.

identifiers.$comment: NimbusStack's own release line — the thing 'what's in Vault 4.2?' asks about. The negative lookbehind is the whole point: without it 'SAML 2.0', 'TLS 1.2' and 'Datadog Agent 7.40' were indexed as product versions, so Vault appeared to have a version 2.0 and Relay a 7.40. Harmless while identifiers were only a ranking bonus; dangerous once an ABSENT identifier vetoes a query, because a mis-extracted one can then refuse a good question.
SAML 2.0, TLS 1.2, Datadog Agent 7.40. Kept as a real identifier kind rather than discarded, so a question naming one still matches instead of being vetoed as absent.

Loose on the QUERY side ('they receive 403') and strict on the INDEX side (a status code in a document is followed by its reason phrase). Without the split, '400 days' of audit retention and '500' secrets indexed as HTTP codes, and once identifiers vouch that is a way to answer any question containing a three-digit number. Controls ident-404-absent / ident-500-absent pin it.

$identBonusComment: Added to the negated BM25 score when a query identifier matches a chunk identifier. A bonus, deliberately, not a hard filter: 'does Relay 4.2 support Salesforce?' is answered by relay.md#integrations, which carries no 4.2 identifier, and a filter would hide it.
$synonymComment: The most client-specific thing here, and the honest reason it still exists: these documents never contain the strings 'SSO' or 'cheaper' (df = 0 for both), and no tokenizer or stemmer closes a vocabulary gap. Porter stemming subsumes the inflectional patterns the old table carried by hand (price/pricing, integrat*, release*, product*), so only genuine vocabulary mapping is left. These feed RANKING ONLY — see gate.ts, where coverage is computed over literal terms. An expansion can no longer manufacture the evidence that decides whether to answer. The long-term replacement is a dense retrieval arm, which learns this mapping instead of being told it.
$thresholdComment: BUCKET C's calibration. These are not opinions — run `npm run eval -- --sweep` and read the table. Every value here is the measured minimum-error point on eval/nimbusstack.jsonl, and the sweep prints the false-grounding / false-refusal tradeoff either side of it so the choice is visible rather than asserted.

thresholds.$coverageComment: The refusal gate. IDF-weighted fraction of the user's LITERAL query terms that the corpus covers, 0..1. Replaces an absolute count of 2 matched terms, which was not scale-free: an absolute bar against a growing corpus opens over time. An out-of-vocabulary term counts at MAXIMUM idf in the DENOMINATOR, so 'landlord' drags coverage toward zero instead of being silently skipped. CALIBRATED, NOT CHOSEN — `npm run eval -- --sweep` on 2026-10-17 over 82 labelled cases: 0.15 -> 0/57 false refusals, 10/25 false groundings; 0.20 -> 0/57, 8/25; 0.30 -> 0/57, 6/25; 0.35 -> 0/57, 5/25 (minimum error, 76/82 cases); 0.40 -> 1/57, 5/25; 0.50 -> 3/57, 3/25. 0.35 is the last point before false refusals start, and false groundings are the dangerous failure. Re-run the sweep after any corpus change rather than trusting this number.
thresholds.$relevanceFloorComment: Ratio to the best score, for trimming the tail within one query. Kept because it is measurably harmless and cheap, not because it is principled: BM25 scores are not calibrated across queries, so this measures score spread. It is a tail-trimmer, and the coverage gate above is what actually decides refusal.
thresholds.$maxConflictsComment: Raised 3 -> 5 on 2026-10-17. The real Vault SAML contradiction was being sliced off behind three co-mentions (passages that merely both say SAML). The detector ranks SHARED RARE TERMS, which is not the same as ranking contradiction — it cannot see that security-overview#identity makes a claim about Vault specifically, because that claim is a table ROW inside a company-wide document whose chunk-level product is null. Widening the slice is a workaround with a stated cost (more noise in the prompt note); the real fix is an offline conflict registry with a human-adjudicated winner, which is the >200-chunk trigger.
thresholds.$rrfKComment: Reciprocal Rank Fusion constant. 60 is the value from the original RRF paper and is not sensitive; it damps the head of each ranking so one arm cannot dominate.
thresholds.$denseFloorComment: Semantic coverage: the cosine similarity at which the dense arm vouches for a query that the LEXICAL coverage gate would refuse. THIS IS THE POINT OF THE DENSE ARM — it is what should let the synonym table shrink, because an embedding already knows sell~products and cheaper~pricing. Calibrate with `npm run eval -- --sweep-dense`.
thresholds.$identVouchesComment: A MATCHED typed identifier vouches for the query, overriding lexical coverage. Identifiers are high-precision by construction. Measured 2026-10-17: without it, 'a client said they receive 403' scored coverage 0.25 and was refused — 'client', 'said' and 'receive' appear nowhere in the corpus, so one matched code was outvoted by three absent words. It vouches only on a MATCH, so 'what's in Vault 4.2?' is still correctly refused.
thresholds.$identVetoesComment: The symmetric counterpart of identVouches: a typed identifier the corpus does NOT contain refuses the query outright. Identifiers are high-precision in both directions — naming an undocumented error code is stronger evidence than any incidental prose match. Without it, 401 and 404 (both undocumented) got opposite verdicts purely because 'user' appears in a troubleshooting section and 'client' does not. Fires only when NOTHING the reader named was found, so a query naming both a documented and an undocumented identifier still answers the documented part.

$embeddingComment: The dense arm. BUILT, MEASURED, AND LEFT OFF — the measurement is the deliverable. HEAD-TO-HEAD on 93 labelled cases, denseFloor 0.58, 2026-10-17: ON  -> 84/93, recall 0.978, MRR 0.790, 1 false refusal, 7 false groundings, 5.5 passages/answer. OFF -> 84/93, recall 0.978, MRR 0.777, 1 false refusal, 7 false groundings, 5.2 passages/answer. Per-query diff: ZERO outcome flips across all 93; ~35 passage-set changes, most of them the dense arm ADDING irrelevant passages to precise single-cell lookups — 'how many seats are included with Relay Pro?' gained security-overview#identity, a release note and an SLA table. It dilutes citation precision on exactly the questions where a reader is checking one table cell mid-call, and buys +0.013 MRR, which is noise. Threshold sweep: identical to off at 0.58/0.60/0.65/0.70; actively harmful below (0.45 -> 10 false groundings, 0.40 -> 15). Ablation of 'embeddings replace the synonym table': with synonyms removed it recovered 1 of 6 vocabulary cases. WHY: measured cosine distributions overlap — answerable median 0.574, should-refuse p90 0.509 / max 0.567. Above the junk tail it stops firing for real vocabulary gaps too. At 38 short chunks nearly every query finds SOME passage at moderate similarity; the discrimination dense retrieval needs comes from having enough documents that a true match stands out. TURN IT ON WHEN: the corpus passes ~300 chunks, or the eval shows false refusals driven by vocabulary the synonym table cannot reach. Then re-run `npm run eval -- --sweep-dense`; do not trust this comment, it describes a 38-chunk corpus. TO FLIP: set enabled:true AND re-run `npm run build:index` — the vectors live in the index, and a build with enabled:false leaves that table empty. The rebuild costs no API call because vectors are cached by content hash in <client>.vectors.json. BETTER SECOND MOVE than raw cosine: a cross-encoder reranker, which reads query and passage together. UNCONTROLLED VARIABLE: text-embedding-3-small at 256 dimensions; 1536 dims or a stronger model might separate better, untested.
